title: The Standard Library
instructions: C comes with ready-made toolboxes (libraries). You #include a toolbox, then use its tools instead of reinventing them.
- <ctype.h> for characters: toupper('a') gives 'A'; isdigit('7') asks 'is this a digit?'
- <stdlib.h> for utilities: atoi("42") turns the text "42" into the number 42.
Knowing a library exists saves you from writing code that's already been written and tested for you.
The habit to build: before writing something fiddly, check if the standard library already does it.
task: Add the atoi call that turns "42" into a number, so the output ends with:  number + 1 = 43
hint:
Use atoi to convert text to a number:

    int number = atoi("42");
